confirmed.statement: S1 explicitly assigns participants by block randomization to four cells of a preregistered, between-subjects 2 x 2 factorial experiment. This is individual assignment; randomized within-person condition order is inapplicable.
AI assistance itself was randomized: "Apart from randomizing AI assistance, we also randomized participants into two conditions:" followed by originality (O) versus technical quality (T).

AI participants received an integrated assistant for producing their own short stories; SELF participants wrote entirely on their own. Assignment concerned assistance during writing, not whose output participants evaluated.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 4, Section 3.2.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4.

confirmed.statement: The generative tool is identified as OpenAI's GPT5-Mini and, in the appendix, gpt5-mini with medium reasoning. It provides open chat beside the editor, including generated drafts and edits.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 1, Introduction, "The present work"; p. 5, "AI Usage"; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4.

confirmed.statement: AI was unavailable during initial brainstorming and available during writing. AI participants had to prompt at least once, could make up to 15 calls, could decline all suggestions, and could copy-paste within their study window.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 3.2.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4; p. 25, Appendix A.2, "Window-specific strategies."

confirmed.statement: SELF-O and SELF-T used only the editor and were forbidden external AI; AI-O and AI-T used the provided assistant. AI versus SELF contrasts therefore match the form's no-AI comparator.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2; p. 18, Appendix A.1.1; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4.

confirmed.statement: The two AI arms share the assistant configuration and differ in incentives; the two SELF arms likewise differ in incentives. The form correctly distinguishes these incentive-only contrasts from AI-versus-no-AI contrasts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 4, Sections 3.2.1-3.2.2 and Table 1; p. 18, Appendix A.1.2; p. 20, Appendix A.1.4.

confirmed.statement: The originality rubric promises $7 for the top 2%, $4 for the top 2-10%, and $2 for the top 10-25%. The technical rubric promises $2.50 for A and $1.00 for B, assessing organization and technique while excluding creativity.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 19, Figure 8, both embedded instruction images inspected directly; also p. 18, Appendix A.1.2.

confirmed.statement: The actual bonus was $1 for every completed work, paid after the study; the form correctly separates actual payment from announced incentive conditions.
The reported sample has 200 participants and 50 in each named cell. The paper also reports 29 exclusions without an explicit total randomized, supporting the form's null randomized counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 5, Table 2 and caption; p. 25, Appendix A.2.

confirmed.statement: The tool-use figures match: 3.57 mean conversation turns; 91% requested a full draft; requests comprised editing 38%, drafting 30%, creative consulting 14%, mechanical assistance 3%, and other 15%.

summary: The PDF explicitly supports random assignment to GPT5-mini assistance versus writing alone, crossed with incentive type. The form's assignment, arm, and tool coding is supported, and criterion 1 holds.
